newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn attacked over liquidation of east German SKET.
newsitem.headline: Bonn attacked over liquidation of east German SKET.

text.p: The German government came under opposition fire on Friday for allowing liquidation proceedings to open against east Germany's SKET GmbH, the former communist region's largest heavy machinery company.
In a parliamentary debate called by the PDS, the reformed east German communists, opposition leaders slammed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government for going back on promises to help save SKET.
Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt replied that management had no other choice after SKET's 1,850 workers refused to back a cost-cutting plan to reduce the workforce by two-thirds.
Over one billion marks in state aid has been ploughed into SKET since reunification but, Rexrodt said, targets under a management rescue plan last April had been hopelessly missed.
Rexrodt said that SKET, under the control of the BvS, a successor to the Treuhand privatisation agency, could only be saved if it was privatised, but finding a buyer would be tough.
Helmut Buettner, of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said liquidation would be a "last chance" for SKET, which expects to lose 190 million marks this year on turnover of 120 million marks.
SKET, which has suffered from a collapse in its traditional east European markets, employed 18,000 before German reunification in 1990.
Wolf Schoede, spokesman for the BvS, said that it would be possible to save Magdeburg-based SKET.
Talks with European Union competition commissioner Karel Van Miert are planned for next week, as are meetings between the BvS and SKET managers, Schoede said in a statement.
